chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazeed ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about ill-gotten gain (al-suh't), so he said: 'The bribe in judgement.'

key_terms.الرِّشْوَةُ: Bribe; payment given to influence a decision
key_terms.السُّحْت: Ill-gotten gain; wealth consumed unjustly or unlawfully

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Suh't (ill-gotten gain) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) equates 'al-suh't' with 'al-rihsha' (bribe) specifically within the context of judicial rulings, highlighting how corruption undermines the integrity of legal verdicts. This definition is significant in Shia jurisprudence for categorizing bribery as a form of consuming wealth unjustly, distinct from general trade or consumption. The hadith serves as a foundational text for scholars analyzing the invalidity of bribes in court proceedings and their impact on the legitimacy of judicial decisions.
